summary:
Your 4-week volume sits at 113 km, down 9% from the prior block, but the June 8 effort — 44 km at 5:53/km with 442m elevation — anchors the recent period as a genuine durability session rather than maintenance work. That run alone represents the kind of long-term base currency that doesn't evaporate across a few lighter weeks.

The June 27 run is the more analytically interesting data point: 15.7 km at 4:49/km with HR 161 is a meaningful intensity signal, sitting well below your half-marathon PB pace but at a load of 239 — your highest since the June 8 long effort. Paired with today's LT assessment of 4:24/km at 178 bpm, you have a credible current speed ceiling to work from, and the 4:49 session sits comfortably within productive threshold-adjacent range rather than junk zone.

Today's LT result is the first formal data point in this tracking window, so there's no 30-day comparison available yet — but 4:24/km at 178 bpm is consistent with someone carrying both a sub-4:00/km 5K and a 44 km trail effort in recent history. It will be worth noting whether subsequent assessments trend faster, slower, or flat as the summer block develops.

Your daily step average of 14,120 over the last 28 days — including 11,641 on rest days — reflects the kind of background movement load that tends to be invisible in run metrics but materially supports aerobic base and connective tissue maintenance. At 4 strength sessions in the last 4 weeks, the lifting consistency is present but at the lower edge of what sustains meaningful adaptation; watch whether the 3-week streak holds through the next training cycle.
